source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.leaves: Usually (1–)2–3 pinna pairs; ultimate leaflets fold at night or when touched
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Petals united to about halfway, conspicuous pink filaments
morphology_source_reported.fruits: Mostly 4-sided to nearly cylindrical, 2–4 mm wide [key]; not strongly flattened
morphology_source_reported.diagnostic_characters: Sandy-soil trailing sensitive-briar with more cylindrical pods, as contrasted with flattened fruit of M. roemeriana

cautions: Flora recognizes species rank and discusses competing Mimosa quadrivalvis varietal classification; retain as historical-source concept, not independent modern taxonomy
Source morphology has not been independently corroborated or approved for identification scoring
Regional habitat and distribution do not establish Hays County nativity
